items.text: Thanks so much for the detailed write-up! I've passed your notes on the export screen to our product team and linked them to your account.
items.label: good

items.text: Enterprise doesn't have a list price; it's priced on a custom basis, so I've asked our sales team to contact you directly.
items.label: good

items.text: If you switch to annual billing, Pro comes to $41.20 a month.

items.text: Since you're on the Pro plan, I've added the 15% loyalty discount to your next invoice.

items.text: Thank you for two years with Lumen Cloud. As a long-time Starter customer, you're now eligible for our 15% loyalty discount.
items.label: bad
items.reason: The loyalty discount applies only to Pro and Business. Tenure is long enough, but Starter is not an eligible plan.

items.text: I've applied both your loyalty discount and the annual billing discount to your Business renewal, so you'll see the two reductions together on the invoice.

items.text: Upgrading to Enterprise is a flat $299 per month, billed the same way as your current plan.
items.label: bad
items.reason: Enterprise has custom pricing through sales; there is no flat $299 price.

items.text: As a Business customer, you'll get a first response from our team within 1 hour.
items.label: bad
items.reason: Business first response is 4 hours on the price sheet; 1 hour over-promises the response time.

items.text: I checked with the product team: single sign-on for Starter accounts is coming, and it will be live before your renewal in March.
items.label: bad
items.reason: Promises a product feature and a delivery date, which agents are not authorized to do. Not provably false, so a manager reviews it.

items.text: I've approved a one-time exception for you, so your refund will go through even though the request came in after the refund window closed.
items.label: bad
items.reason: Grants an exception outside the refund policy. The email states the policy correctly and makes an exception to it, which is a manager decision, not a factual contradiction.

items.text: INCREDIBLE deal!!! Business is $99 a month with a 4-hour first response, the BEST support you'll ever get!!
items.label: bad
items.reason: Price and response time are correct, but the tone is over-the-top promotional (exclamation marks, all-caps, hype words). Overall tier stays GREEN while tone is very low.

items.text: Under the GDPR, you can ask us to delete your personal data. Just reply from the email address on your account and our privacy team will pick it up from there.
items.label: good
items.reason: Ezio reports the GDPR deletion-right claim as supported. The company files are silent on it, which is not a reason to hold.

items.text: Thanks for your message. Lumen Cloud is based in the U.S., and the GDPR only applies to companies headquartered in the EU, so we can't act on your erasure request.
items.label: bad
items.reason: Ezio reports the claim that the GDPR applies only to EU-headquartered companies as contradicted. Only Ezio's fact-check catches this.

items.text: We suspended the site because one of its posts was inciting imminent lawless action against a named person, which isn't protected speech. You can appeal the decision through the abuse portal.
items.label: good
items.reason: Ezio supports the claim that speech inciting imminent lawless action is not protected. No company-data claims to check.

items.text: The First Amendment protects free speech from government restriction, but as a private hosting provider we still enforce our acceptable use policy, which is why the page was taken down.
items.label: good
items.reason: Ezio supports the First Amendment claim. Nothing in it touches prices or policies, so it should be sent.

items.text: Your subscription price isn't tied to interest rates. On your side question, the SEC sets the federal funds rate, so any rate changes come from them rather than from us.
items.label: bad
items.reason: Ezio reports 'the SEC sets the federal funds rate' as contradicted (the FOMC does). The company files cannot see this.

items.text: You can ask us to delete your personal data whenever you like, and if you cancel within 60 days of your first monthly payment you'll get a full refund.
items.label: bad
items.reason: Ezio supports the GDPR deletion claim, but the monthly refund window is 30 days, not 60. A supported public claim does not excuse a wrong company fact.

items.text: Starter tickets get a first response within 24 hrs.

items.text: Pro is $49 a month, comes with a free trial lasting a fortnight, and includes a first response within 4 hours.
items.label: bad
items.reason: Price and trial are right, but Pro's first response is 24 hours (4 hours is Business). Exactly one wrong fact among three.

items.text: Moving from pro to business is easy: pro is $49 and business is $79 a month, so you'd only pay $30 more.
items.label: bad
items.reason: Business is $99 per month, not $79 ($79.20 is its annual per-month price). Lowercase plan names in a two-plan comparison.

items.text: Good news about your annual plan: you have thirty days from the first payment to ask for a full refund.
items.label: bad
items.reason: Annual plans are refundable within 14 days; 30 days is the monthly-plan window. Figure written in words.

items.text: Pro is forty-nine dollars a month, and I guarantee your pages will never go down again once you upgrade.
items.label: bad
items.reason: The price is right (written in words), but the agent guarantees uptime, a promise the agent cannot make. No hype word or exclamation, so Ezio's tone stays high.

items.text: Just so you know, the loyalty discount and the annual billing discount can't be combined, so you'll need to choose one of the two.
items.label: good
items.reason: Correctly states the no-stacking rule; the negation must not be read as a stacking claim.

items.text: No credit card is required to start the 14-day Business trial; you can add payment details later if you decide to stay.
items.label: good
items.reason: Business has a 14-day trial and no card is required.

items.text: Starter doesn't include a free trial. The 14-day trial is only available on the Pro and Business plans.
items.label: good
items.reason: Starter has no trial; Pro and Business have 14 days. The negation must not be read as 'Starter has a 14-day trial'.

items.text: Your refund for the first Pro payment has been issued. Depending on your bank, it usually takes 5-7 business days to appear on your statement.
items.label: good
items.reason: Bank processing time is not the refund-eligibility window; the policy is silent on it, so there is nothing to contradict. The refund itself is for the first payment within 30 days.

items.text: I'm checking the charge with our billing team now and I'll get back to you within 2 hours with an answer.
items.label: good
items.reason: A personal follow-up on an open conversation, not a statement of the plan's first-response time, and not a feature or delivery promise.

items.text: I can't promise a date for the dark-mode dashboard, but I've shared your request with the product team and will update this ticket if anything changes.
items.label: good
items.reason: Explicitly declines to promise a feature date; this is the honest behavior the rules want.
